Subject: Discovery recap: audit & redaction constraints + next steps

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call with AlderBio's data engineering and compliance leads (notes below) and proposed next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points / goals
- Sensitive outputs from model-powered assistants are showing up in observability traces and Sentry events; compliance requires narrower logging and demonstrable redaction for PII.
- Retention policy: logs containing PII must be retained for 1 year in encrypted storage, non-PII telemetry for 90 days.
- Auditability: must produce exportable, tamper-evident audit logs for all inference requests tied to request IDs and model version.
- Success criteria: Redwood can (1) prevent PII from being stored in plaintext in logs, (2) provide per-request audit events and retention controls, and (3) integrate with AlderBio's KMS for key wrapping.

Current stack (what we heard)
- Inference currently hosted on internal Kubernetes with Sentry for error traces and ELK for logs.
- Customer uses HashiCorp Vault for secrets and AWS KMS for data encryption.
- Post-processing redaction is done via a homegrown pipeline (Python Lambda) that flags tokens based on regex + lookup tables. This pipeline is error-prone and adds latency.

Initial technical considerations for Redwood
- We believe Redwood Dedicated can be configured to not emit model outputs to system logs and to surface structured audit events instead.
- Options for redaction: (a) inline token redaction prior to any log sink, (b) prefix caching with token filtering, or (c) post-request redact-only audit pipeline with strong guarantees (we prefer option a for lowest surface).
- KMS integration: support for AWS KMS and external key wraps; will validate HSM/KMS workflows during technical review.

Proposed next steps (action items)
1) Marcus to prepare a short technical note showing how Redwood will block model output from application logs and what audit events we can emit (due Thu 05/20).
2) Emily to share AlderBio's redact-spec (example regexes / data classes) and a sanitized sample event (anonymized) for verification.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with AlderBio infra + security (30–45m) next week to validate KMS and audit export formats.
4) Add Monica from our CS team for retention/SLA discussion once we align on audit shape.

Attachments: alderbio-redaction-requirements-v1.pdf (attachment stub)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the tech note and a calendar invite.

Best,
Priyom Das

Redwood Inference

Priyom — thanks for the crisp recap, that's exactly right. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- The retention window for PII is actually 13 months (to align with our HR policy); non-PII telemetry 90 days still stands.
- For audit logs we need an exportable CSV or JSONL that includes request_id, model_version, timestamp, and a redaction_status flag (redacted / not_redacted).
- We're open to inline redaction but need to see a low-latency design; our users tolerate up to 150ms additional latency on tail requests.

I attached a redacted sample (sanitized) and our redact-spec doc. Can Marcus and team confirm whether inline filtering will require model change or can be enforced at the serving runtime?

Emily

Hi Emily — appreciate the sample and the extra detail. Short technical responses below; happy to dig deeper on the call.

1) Inline redaction feasibility
- Inline token redaction can be implemented at the serving/runtime layer without modifying base model weights. Our runtime supports a policy hook that inspects and mutates generated tokens before they hit any log or trace exporter. That hook can apply regex and entity-match lists; it's executed in-memory on the token stream.
- Latency: we estimate median overhead of ~10–30ms for typical prompts; worst-case pathological regex sets could add ~120ms. We'll send a micro-benchmark.

2) Audit events and export format
- We can emit structured audit events per request (JSONL) with the fields you requested: request_id, model_version, timestamp, redaction_status. Events are signed (HMAC) to support tamper evidence.

3) Retention controls and KMS
- Redwood can tag audit events and route them to a customer-configured S3 bucket with lifecycle rules (object lock optional). We support KMS key wrapping and can integrate with external key APIs; we'll validate your Vault + AWS KMS flow on the deep-dive.

Actionables
- I'll attach a short note with benchmarks and a sample JSONL audit export (proposed). Expect that by EOD Thu 05/20.
- Can we schedule the deep-dive Tue 05/25 or Wed 05/26? Priyom, can you coordinate times with AlderBio?
